writing.prompt:
Part I Writing (30 minutes)

Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on why mental health deserves as much attention as physical health. You can cite examples to illustrate your point. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.ideas: 审题思路:现象分析类。结构:① 首段用对比破题:骨折人人重视,抑郁却常被当作「想开点就行」,双重标准源于看不见伤口;② 理由一:身心一体,长期压力会真实地损伤身体(失眠、免疫力下降、心血管风险);③ 理由二:心理问题具有隐蔽性和累积性,越晚干预代价越大,而早期关注成本极低;④ 结尾给行动建议:像年度体检一样做心理体检,把求助正常化。
writing.model:
When someone breaks an arm, the whole office signs the cast. When someone admits to months of anxiety, the same office goes quiet. This double standard persists because bones show and minds do not—yet the evidence says mental health deserves exactly the same attention as physical health.
The first reason is that the two are not separate systems. Chronic stress keeps the body flooded with hormones that raise blood pressure, weaken immunity and disrupt sleep; doctors now describe depression as a whole-body condition, not merely a mood. Ignoring the mind therefore does not protect the body; it simply delays the bill.
The second reason is the economics of intervention. A sprained ankle treated early costs an ice pack; treated late, it costs months of physiotherapy. The same curve applies to psychological strain, but far more steeply: a student who talks to a counsellor in week one rarely becomes a dropout in month six. What makes early help unlikely is stigma—the belief that struggling means weakness. It takes courage to book a therapy session, and a society that treats that courage as ordinary gets healthier citizens for free.
Mental check-ups, like physical ones, should be routine rather than remedial. The cast is visible; the strain is not. Both deserve a doctor.
writing.notes: 亮点:① 开头 cast 与 quiet 的场景对比,画面感强;② whole-body condition 替代枯燥的 psychosomatic;③ the economics of intervention 用经济学视角重构健康投入;④ 结尾 Both deserve a doctor 回环首段,克制有力。加分表达:delays the bill, the economics of intervention, routine rather than remedial。

listening.intro:
Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

【听力原文】
W: Our dorm had a two-hour argument last night about whether universities should ban delivery robots.
M: And did anyone change their mind?
W: Nobody, of course. But my roommate said something useful afterwards: we were not discussing, we were competing.
M: There is a difference?
W: Huge. In a discussion, you listen to understand; in a competition, you listen to find the gap to attack. Last night we all did the second.
M: So what should we have done?
W: Each person states their view, then has to summarise the previous speaker accurately before replying. Our professor calls it "steel-manning"—presenting the other side at its strongest.
M: Sounds painfully slow.
W: It is. But it is the only way two people end a conversation having learned something instead of just having talked.
listening.questions:
1. What did the dorm argue about?
A) Banning delivery robots.
B) Homework deadlines.
C) Roommate rules.
D) Professor grading.

2. What did the roommate say they were actually doing?
A) Discussing.
B) Competing.
C) Studying.
D) Complaining.

3. What is "steel-manning"?
A) Attacking the weakest point.
B) Summarising the other side at its strongest.
C) Interrupting politely.
D) Agreeing with everything.

4. Why does the woman support the slow method?
A) It ends arguments faster.
B) It impresses professors.
C) People learn something instead of just talking.
D) It avoids all conflict.
listening.analysis:
1. A。首句:宿舍争论大学是否应禁止送货机器人(delivery robots)。
2. B。室友事后点破:他们不是在讨论,而是在竞争(competing)。
3. B。steel-manning 指先准确概括对方观点、并以最强形式呈现再回应。
4. C。女士认为只有这样,对话结束时双方才真正学到东西,而不只是说了一堆话。

listening.intro:
Questions 5 to 7 are based on the passage you have just heard.

【听力原文】
Ask a room of students how they study and most will describe rereading notes and highlighting textbooks. Ask them how well it works and most will admit: not very. Educational psychologists have a name for the gap between what feels effective and what is effective—the illusion of fluency.
Rereading makes text feel familiar, and familiarity is easily mistaken for knowledge. But when the book is closed, very little can be retrieved. Far better techniques feel clumsier: closing the book and writing down everything you remember; explaining the concept to an imaginary twelve-year-old; spacing study sessions across days instead of hours.
One university went so far as to teach these techniques explicitly in a first-year course. Students who completed it earned higher grades in subsequent courses, and—more importantly—kept using the methods two years later. The researchers' conclusion is blunt: learning how to learn is not a soft skill picked up along the way. It is a skill that must be taught, deliberately, early, and often.
listening.questions:
5. What do most students say about their study methods?
A) They are highly effective.
B) They do not work very well.
C) They are research-based.
D) They use spacing.

6. Why is rereading ineffective?
A) It takes too long.
B) Familiarity is mistaken for knowledge.
C) It requires a textbook.
D) It bores students.

7. What happened to students who took the learning-to-learn course?
A) They dropped out.
B) They earned higher grades later and kept using the methods.
C) They stopped studying.
D) They taught the course themselves.
listening.analysis:
5. B。多数学生承认方法不太管用(not very)。
6. B。重读带来熟悉感,而熟悉感容易被误认为知识——即「流畅性错觉」。
7. B。修过该课程的学生后续课程成绩更高,且两年后仍在沿用这些方法。

listening.intro:
Questions 8 to 10 are based on the lecture you have just heard.

【听力原文】
Tonight's lecture will, I hope, send you to bed earlier. Sleep science has advanced dramatically in the past decade, and three findings deserve wide publicity.
First, memory consolidation happens largely during deep sleep. Students who sleep after studying outperform those who stay awake reviewing—by margins that grow when the sleep includes a full ninety-minute cycle. Second, the glymphatic system, discovered only in 2012, acts as the brain's cleaning crew, flushing metabolic waste during sleep; some researchers suspect that chronic sleep deprivation raises the risk of dementia precisely because the cleaning crew never finishes its shift. Third, and most practically, caffeine has a half-life of about five hours, which means the coffee you drink at four p.m. is still a quarter active at nine.
The conclusion is not that sleep is a luxury for the disciplined. Sleep is the period during which yesterday's learning becomes tomorrow's ability, and the brain's maintenance team clocks in. Treat it as a class you cannot skip.
listening.questions:
8. When does memory consolidation mainly happen?
A) During light sleep.
B) During deep sleep.
C) While awake.
D) While exercising.

9. What is the glymphatic system's function?
A) Producing dreams.
B) Flushing metabolic waste from the brain.
C) Storing memories.
D) Regulating caffeine.

10. What is caffeine's half-life?
A) About one hour.
B) About two hours.
C) About five hours.
D) About ten hours.
listening.analysis:
8. B。记忆巩固主要发生在深睡阶段。
9. B。类淋巴系统于 2012 年被发现,负责在睡眠中清除大脑代谢废物。
10. C。咖啡因半衰期约五小时,下午四点的咖啡到晚上九点仍有四分之一在起作用。

reading.title: The Quiet Power of Boredom
reading.passage:
Parents used to complain that their children were bored; now they compete to ensure it never happens. Every idle moment is filled with a screen, every wait in a queue becomes a game, and boredom—the state that once launched a thousand daydreams—has been engineered out of childhood. A growing body of research suggests this is a mistake with measurable costs.
Psychologists distinguish between two states that look similar from outside. One is genuine boredom: an under-stimulated mind with nothing to do. The other is constant low-grade distraction. The first, experiments show, reliably produces creativity—given nothing to react to, the mind manufactures its own material, and participants allowed to be bored before a creative task outperform those primed with entertainment. The second state, however, consumes attention without generating anything, and it is the second state that screens supply.
The developmental stakes are highest for children. Boredom is how the young learn to entertain themselves, to invent games, to tolerate stillness. A child who never experiences it arrives at university unable to sit through a lecture that does not deliver a dopamine hit every ninety seconds. The capacity for sustained attention, it turns out, is not a trait some are born with; it is a muscle that unused minds never build.
None of this requires abandoning screens. It requires restoring the gaps: car rides without videos, queues without phones, evenings with nothing scheduled. Boredom is not the enemy of a good mind. It is the soil the good mind grows in.
reading.questions:
1. What did parents used to complain about?
A) Their children studied too much.
B) Their children were bored.
C) Their children used screens.
D) Their children invented games.

2. What does the passage say about genuine boredom?
A) It causes anxiety.
B) It reliably produces creativity.
C) It wastes time.
D) It should be avoided.

3. What state do screens mainly supply?
A) Genuine boredom.
B) Restful stillness.
C) Constant low-grade distraction.
D) Creative daydreaming.

4. What happens to children who never experience boredom?
A) They become more creative.
B) They cannot sit through lectures without stimulation.
C) They sleep better.
D) They invent more games.

5. What is the passage's conclusion?
A) Screens should be banned.
B) Boredom is the soil a good mind grows in.
C) Children need more games.
D) Attention is a fixed trait.
reading.analysis:
1. B。第一段:过去父母常抱怨孩子无聊(children were bored)。
2. B。第二段:真正的无聊能可靠地激发创造力,实验中被允许无聊的被试在创造性任务上表现更好。
3. C。屏幕提供的是持续的低强度 distraction,消耗注意力却不产生任何东西。
4. B。从未体验无聊的孩子到了大学无法忍受没有频繁刺激的讲座。
5. B。结尾:无聊不是好头脑的敌人,而是好头脑生长的土壤。

translation.prompt:
请将以下中文段落翻译成英文:

中医是中华民族数千年医学实践的结晶,形成了独特的理论体系。强调整体观念和辨证论治,注重人体自身的统一性以及人与自然、社会环境的相互关系。针灸、中药、推拿等疗法已被列入联合国教科文组织人类非物质文化遗产名录。目前,中医药已传播到一百八十多个国家和地区,越来越多的外国人开始接受并信赖这种古老而有效的医疗体系。
translation.reference: Traditional Chinese medicine is the culmination of China's medical practice over thousands of years and has developed a unique theoretical system. It emphasises a holistic view and treatment based on syndrome differentiation, attaching importance to the unity of the human body itself as well as its interrelations with nature and the social environment. Therapies such as acupuncture, herbal medicine and tuina (therapeutic massage) have been inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Today, traditional Chinese medicine has spread to more than 180 countries and regions, and a growing number of foreigners have come to accept and trust this ancient yet effective medical system.
translation.notes: 要点:①「结晶」译为 culmination,正式且准确;②「辨证论治」是中医术语,固定译法 treatment based on syndrome differentiation;③「推拿」可用拼音 tuina 并加注 therapeutic massage;④「非物质文化遗产名录」注意使用 UNESCO 官方名称 Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity;⑤「古老而有效」用 ancient yet effective 连接,比 and 更紧凑。
